title: RFC 4103 ↔ RFC 8865 T.140 semantic equivalence
objective: Demonstrate that a two-party T.140 conversation preserves the same presentation-level text semantics when interworked between RFC 4103 RTP/RED and an RFC 8865 reliable ordered T.140 data channel, while keeping transport-specific reliability mechanisms on their own side of the gateway.
scope: This version is runnable through Baudot's deterministic reference gateway harness. It proves executable semantic composition of the repository's reference adapters; it does not establish live network, browser, SIP, production gateway, or full protocol conformance.

supersedes.reason: The v1 planning contract's deterministic adapter and normalized gateway-harness gates are now executable in-repository.

basis: normal T140blocks are forwarded between RTP-based and data-channel T.140 transports
RTP redundancy is used by default on the RFC 4103 side while the T.140 data channel has no redundancy
unrecovered or suspected RTP loss should be represented by a T.140 missing-text marker on the outgoing data channel
suspected loss across data-channel failure/reestablishment should be represented by a T.140 missing-text marker on the outgoing transport
the same text transmission direction must be indicated on both sides

invariants: normal T.140 content is preserved across the transport boundary
RFC 2198 redundancy metadata never becomes T.140 application content on the data-channel side
data-channel reliability is not represented as synthetic RFC 2198 history on the WebRTC side
an unrecovered missing T140block is represented by U+FFFD before forwarding to the opposite transport
an empty T140block is not converted into a missing-text marker
text transmission direction is preserved across the gateway
presentation semantics are compared after transport-specific recovery and before transport-specific re-encoding
transport packet or message boundaries are not required to remain identical when presentation semantics are equivalent

trials.condition: all RFC 4103 primary T140blocks available after any RED processing
one lost RFC 4103 primary T140block is recovered from RFC 2198 redundancy
one lost RFC 4103 primary T140block remains unrecovered after available redundancy
the T.140 data channel is reestablished and the gateway detects or suspects intervening text loss
an empty RFC 4103 T140block occurs between non-empty T140blocks and is recovered or received normally

evidenceRequiredBeforeProven: preserved presentation result from the shared T.140 reducer
preserved explicit missing-marker count and reason
live independent transport execution beyond the in-process reference harness
